data.title: Tag
data.tagline: Mark a status, category, or selected condition with short text
data.description: Tags help people recognize status, category, and active filters at a glance. Color can support scanning, but the words still need to carry the meaning. A normal tag displays information; a removable tag may clear a filter or selection.

use: Label a small piece of metadata
avoid: Put a sentence inside a tag
Rely on color without a readable label
Use many decorative tags that add no information
Make a display-only tag look removable

lessonPractice.title: An order list shows statuses such as Paid, while the filter area shows active choices Beijing and This month. How should tags work?

options.label: Keep status tags informational and give selected filter tags an explicit remove action
options.feedback: Both use short text for scanning, but only removable filter conditions need a close action. Status is not a button.

options.label: Make every status and filter tag a button that changes order status when clicked
options.feedback: A status tag describes an existing result and should not imply direct editing. Mixing labels and actions invites mistakes.

options.label: Replace every status and filter with colored dots and only show the matching count
options.feedback: Counts cannot replace meanings such as Paid or Beijing, and color dots alone do not identify the active condition.

data.agentPrompt: Standardize order tags: status tags only display the current state and are not clickable; active filter tags can be removed individually and must retain text rather than relying on color. Verify that removing a filter never changes an order's status.
